overview: This Senate resolution congratulates the Philadelphia Eagles on winning Super Bowl LIX, defeating the Kansas City Chiefs 40 to 22 in New Orleans on February 9, 2025, for the team's second Super Bowl title. It recounts highlights from the game, including quarterback Jalen Hurts being named Most Valuable Player and a defense that held the Chiefs scoreless in the first half, and notes running back Saquon Barkley's record-setting rushing season. It asks the Secretary of the Senate to send copies to the team's owner, general manager, head coach, and a senior team official. The resolution is ceremonial and does not change any law. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on February 19, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution is a lighthearted way to celebrate a championship that brought pride to the team's players and fans.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
